concepts.heading: Goleman's Four Domains of Emotional Intelligence
concepts.plain: Emotional intelligence means noticing feelings and handling them well.

concepts.heading: The Four Domains
concepts.alt: A guide holding four balloons showing a mirror, a steering wheel, an ear and two linked hands
concepts.plain: Four parts: know your feelings, manage them, read others and handle relationships.

concepts.heading: EQ Is a Skill, Not a Trait
concepts.alt: A guide lifting a small dumbbell shaped like a heart, flexing with a grin
concepts.plain: This is a skill. You can get better at it with practice.

concepts.heading: Why EQ Matters in Every Relationship
concepts.plain: Dating, partnered or with several partners, you need these skills.

checks.prompt: Which domain is described as the foundation of all emotional intelligence?
checks.explanation: Self-awareness. Self-awareness is described as the foundation of all emotional intelligence.

checks.after: EQ Is a Skill, Not a Trait
checks.prompt: Can emotional intelligence change over time?
options: No, you are born with it
Yes, it is a skill you can build
checks.explanation: Yes, it is a skill you can build. One of the most important things to understand about emotional intelligence is that it is not fixed.

5992e693-069d-4699-99db-1cd3ca70120c.takeaway: Handling feelings well is a skill, and you can get better at it.

concepts.heading: Understanding Your Nervous System Through Polyvagal Theory
concepts.plain: Your body has a built-in alarm system that decides if you feel safe.

concepts.heading: The Three States
concepts.alt: A guide standing beside a traffic light with all three lights glowing
concepts.plain: Your body has three modes: calm and connected, fight or flight, and shut down.

concepts.heading: The Window of Tolerance
concepts.alt: A guide standing calmly inside a wide open window frame, sky behind him
concepts.plain: Your "window" is the zone where you can think clearly and stay present.

concepts.heading: Recognizing When You're Outside Your Window
concepts.alt: A guide noticing a thermometer rising in her hand, eyes wide
concepts.plain: Learn your early signs, like a racing heart or going numb.

concepts.heading: Regulation Techniques
concepts.alt: A guide breathing out slowly with eyes closed, one hand on his belly, a leaf floating by
concepts.plain: You can calm down alone, like with slow breathing, or with someone you trust.

concepts.heading: Dysregulation Is Not a Character Flaw
concepts.plain: Getting overwhelmed is your body protecting you. It is not a flaw.

options: The zone where you can still function well
checks.explanation: The zone where you can still function well. The "window of tolerance" describes the zone of nervous system activation where you can function effectively.

checks.prompt: You notice your heart racing in a hard talk. Which tool from the lesson fits?
options: Slow breathing with a longer exhale
checks.explanation: Slow breathing with a longer exhale. Self-regulation (things you can do alone).

f00cc65f-977f-405d-8264-d650dfa597bd.takeaway: When you feel flooded, your body is in alarm mode. Calm the body first, then talk.

concepts.heading: The Science of Emotional Connection
concepts.plain: Small daily moments decide whether a relationship lasts.

concepts.heading: What Are Emotional Bids?
concepts.alt: She points happily at a bird outside, he turns toward her with a smile
concepts.plain: A bid is any small reach for connection, like a comment, a touch or a sigh.

concepts.heading: Three Responses to Bids
concepts.alt: She reaches out a hand and he turns toward her with a warm smile
concepts.plain: You can turn toward a bid, turn away from it, or turn against it.

concepts.heading: Recognizing Bids in Your Relationships
concepts.alt: Two wave for attention from either side while the third looks back and forth
concepts.plain: Bids show up in every relationship. Catch them on purpose.

checks.prompt: Your partner says, "Look at that sunset!" What is that, in Gottman's terms?
checks.explanation: An emotional bid. An emotional bid is any attempt by one person to connect with another — to get attention, affirmation, affection, or any kind of positive engagement.

checks.prompt: Which response to a bid builds connection?
checks.explanation: Turning toward. Turning toward means acknowledging and engaging with the bid.

1e5bcd97-ff56-4138-9b42-8c6fd226efb9.takeaway: Relationships grow when you notice small reaches for connection and turn toward them.

concepts.heading: Owning Your Emotions in Any Relationship
concepts.plain: Your feelings are yours to understand and look after.

concepts.heading: Emotional Responsibility vs. Emotional Caretaking
concepts.alt: A guide carrying her own backpack with a heart on it, declining to take a second backpack offered to her
concepts.plain: Own your feelings. Do not make them someone's job, and do not take on theirs.

concepts.heading: Navigating Jealousy
concepts.alt: A guide looking at a small green-eyed cloud sitting on his shoulder with curiosity
concepts.plain: Jealousy is normal. Treat it as a signal to look at, not an order to obey.

concepts.heading: Compersion
concepts.alt: A guide beaming with joy and clapping as two small hearts dance together nearby
concepts.plain: Compersion is feeling glad that your partner is happy with someone else.

concepts.heading: New Relationship Energy (NRE)
concepts.alt: A guide floating slightly off the ground surrounded by fizzing sparkles and hearts
concepts.plain: New love feels like a rush. Enjoy it, and keep showing up for the people you already have.

concepts.heading: The Skill of Sitting with Discomfort
concepts.alt: A guide sitting calmly on a bench beside a small storm cloud, letting it rain itself out
concepts.plain: You can feel uncomfortable without acting on it straight away.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Support
concepts.plain: Owning your feelings includes asking for help when you need it.

checks.prompt: Your partner comes home glowing after a great date and you feel happy for them. What is that feeling called?
checks.explanation: Compersion. Compersion means feeling joy at your partner's joy, even when it has nothing to do with you.

checks.prompt: Lee can think of nothing but a new partner and forgets plans with others. What is at work?
checks.explanation: New relationship energy. NRE is the intense excitement, infatuation, and preoccupation that often accompanies new romantic connections.

696069c9-d959-4232-a61d-c8cd363fb693.takeaway: Your feelings are yours to look after. Ask for support without handing them to someone else.
